step_goal: Define how HSConfig should compile guide-backed, non-conservative opening-hand claims into a syntax-safe HearthRanger VisionAI `Mulligan.json` that keeps aggressive intent, preserves explicit throw rules, supports documented selector depth, and avoids an unsafe lone wildcard discard fallback.
required_inputs: An ordered mulligan claim plan that separates unconditional keeps, conditional keeps, and explicit throws instead of flattening everything into per-card anchors.
Resolved CardIDs for every concrete card selector used in mulligan rows.
Guide-normalized selector metadata that distinguishes concrete card lists, `DROPn` selectors, plus-combos, duplicate-selector forms, and wildcard fallback intent.
Condition metadata that distinguishes `*`, `coin`, `nocoin`, opening-hand-count equivalents, and opponent-class conditions backed by official JSON condition syntax.
A compiler capability matrix with documented version floors for `hero_class` and duplicate-selector syntax.
Priority metadata so emitted rows preserve guide order and hold-versus-discard intent.
produced_outputs: A strict-JSON `Mulligan.json` with documented top-level keys `GameCardId`, `ConfigComment`, and `Mulligan.values`.
Ordered mulligan rows that use `comment`, `mulligan`, `condition`, and `value` with `hold` or `discard` only.
A suppression or compilation receipt artifact that records unsupported guide claims, version-gated features, and whether wildcard discard fallback was allowed or blocked.
Per-row provenance that maps each emitted row back to guide claims and stable rule identifiers.
documented_capabilities: The official Mulligan documentation supports concrete card selectors, comma-separated hold lists, explicit discard rows, `DROP1`, `DROP2`, `DROP3`, and higher `DROPn` selectors.
The official Mulligan documentation supports plus-combo selectors such as `CARD_A + CARD_B` and `DROP1 + CARD_A`.
The official Mulligan documentation shows a duplicate-selector form for keeping one copy by default and two copies when available, gated to HearthRanger v10.4.5.0 or higher.
The official Mulligan documentation supports `coin` and `nocoin` conditions and also shows the opening-hand-count equivalent `my_hand(count()) == 4` for coin cases.

The official Mulligan documentation supports opponent-class conditions through `opp_hero(count(),warrior=true) > 0` and multi-class `hero_class=warrior | rogue | paladin`, with `hero_class` available in v9.6.0.0 or higher.
The official Mulligan documentation states that hold rules have higher priority than discard rules when rows overlap.
The official JSON-condition documentation supports `AND`, `OR`, `*`, entity collection expressions, opponent hero checks, and filter syntax needed by documented mulligan conditions.
current_hsconfig_support: The current local compiler emits a valid `Mulligan` block with required top-level structure and row keys.
The current local compiler can carry through a `condition` string and an `intent` value from upstream rows, so it can serialize documented conditions if a richer upstream contract already exists.

The current local implementation primarily consumes `mulligan_anchors` keyed by concrete `card_id`, which means the normal path currently models simple per-card hold anchors rather than full selector-level mulligan rules.
The current research and gameplan contract builders reduce mulligan intent to `hold`, `avoid`, or `neutral`, but only `hold` anchors are promoted into the normal mulligan output path.
The current compiler appends an unconditional `mulligan: "*"`, `condition: "*"`, `value: "discard"` fallback by default.
The current compiler sorts rows by `(card_id, rule_id)` instead of preserving source order.
The current package validator checks only row presence and `hold` or `discard` values for mulligan rows; it does not validate selector depth, documented version gates, or wildcard-fallback safety.
observed_gap: HSConfig does not currently model guide claims as ordered mulligan rows with separate selector kinds, so it cannot faithfully compile concrete keeps, explicit throws, `DROPn`, plus-combos, duplicate selectors, coin branches, no-coin branches, and opponent-class branches as first-class rule types.
Negative mulligan guide claims are currently reduced to `avoid` in research contracts, but the normal gameplan-to-mulligan path does not turn them into explicit `discard` rows.

The current compiler only emits concrete card-id rows plus a blanket wildcard discard fallback, so it cannot express non-conservative documented selectors such as `DROP1 + CARD_A` or targeted matchup keeps without a richer upstream rule contract.
The current compiler reorders rows alphabetically by card id, which can weaken guide-authored priority intent even though the design spec requires preserved row order.
The default wildcard discard fallback can be emitted even when HSConfig has not compiled a narrow positive keep plan, which is exactly the failure mode this closure needs to prevent.
aggressive_generation_policy: Compile mulligan rules from an ordered, selector-level plan instead of from card-only anchors.

Emit the strongest documented selector that matches the guide claim: concrete CardID list when the guide names exact cards, `DROPn` when the guide says to keep all cards at a mana band, and plus-combos when the guide describes same-hand combinations.
Emit explicit `discard` rows for guide-backed throw claims instead of collapsing them into `avoid` metadata only.

Compile `coin` and `nocoin` branches directly when the guide claim is explicit, and allow the documented `my_hand(count()) == 4` equivalent only when that translation is intentional and source-backed.
Compile opponent-class clauses only through documented `opp_hero(...)` patterns, using `hero_class` only when the declared version floor supports it.
Preserve overlapping hold and discard rows because official docs say hold outranks discard; do not delete an explicit discard row simply because a broader hold row also exists.
Allow wildcard `discard` fallback only when the guide defines a narrow keep plan and HSConfig has already emitted at least one non-wildcard hold row; never emit a lone wildcard discard row.
If a guide claim cannot be represented with documented selector and condition syntax, suppress it into a report instead of guessing a weaker or broader row.
validation_gates: The result JSON for this research batch must cover every field in `fields.yaml` and pass `validate_json.py`.
Generated `Mulligan.json` must be strict JSON and must keep the official top-level `Mulligan.values` shape.
Every emitted mulligan row must include `comment`, `mulligan`, `condition`, and `value`, and `value` must be only `hold` or `discard`.

Every `mulligan` selector must match a documented selector family: concrete CardID, comma-separated CardID list, `DROPn`, documented plus-combo, documented duplicate-selector form, or wildcard `*` when explicitly allowed by policy.
Every emitted condition must come from documented Mulligan or JSON-condition grammar, including any declared version gates.
Validation must fail if the compiled mulligan output contains a wildcard discard row but no earlier non-wildcard hold row.
Validation must fail if source order was lost between the ordered mulligan plan and emitted runtime rows.
Suppressed claims must be written to a report with raw guide claim text, suppression reason, and source references.
recommended_design_change: Replace the current `mulligan_anchors`-only model with an ordered `mulligan_plan` contract that stores row-level rules such as `rule_id`, `priority_index`, `selector_kind`, `selector_text`, `intent`, `condition`, `version_floor`, `source_claim_ids`, and `allow_wildcard_fallback`.
Teach the research-contract builder to preserve explicit throws and selector-level guide richness instead of collapsing negative claims to `avoid` and positive claims to card-only hold anchors.
Teach the gameplan builder and `compile_mulligan.py` to emit rows in source order, preserve discard rows, and serialize documented selectors beyond raw CardIDs.
Add a dedicated mulligan validator that checks selector grammar, version-gated features, and the rule `wildcard discard requires at least one earlier non-wildcard hold row`.
Write a `mulligan_compilation_receipt.json` or equivalent suppression report so operators can see which guide claims were emitted, downgraded, version-gated, or blocked.
never_autogenerate_without: Official HearthRanger Mulligan documentation and official JSON-condition documentation cited for every selector and condition family that is emitted.
Concrete CardID resolution for every emitted non-`DROPn` selector component.
An ordered guide-backed mulligan plan that distinguishes keep rows, throw rows, selector forms, and conditional branches.
A declared version floor when using `hero_class` or duplicate-selector syntax.
A validation rule that blocks wildcard discard fallback unless at least one earlier non-wildcard hold row exists.
A suppression path for vague or unsupported guide claims rather than silent downgrades.
